q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is 2026-08-23. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release occurred on May 20, 2026 (when they issued forward guidance of $91.0B ±2%). This means the event has **already occurred** — we are now looking back at a historical guidance figure that was announced roughly 3 months ago.

The resolution will be based on the forward guidance NVIDIA actually issued in their Q2 FY2027 earnings release, which according to the research has already happened.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

According to the real-time research provided, NVIDIA issued forward guidance of **$91.0 billion** (±2%) on May 20, 2026 for Q2 FY2027. This guidance is explicitly documented in their official investor relations materials.

The most likely outcome is that the resolution will reflect this already-announced guidance of $91.0 billion. This is not a forecast of what they *will* guide to — it's what they *have already guided to*.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

The guidance ceiling at the lower end is $89.2 billion (representing the -2% margin). However, since this guidance was already issued on May 20, 2026, and we're now on August 23, 2026, the guidance figure itself should not change unless:
- There's confusion about what the actual guidance number was
- Resolution criteria interpret this differently than the official announcement
- The question is asking for something other than the official forward guidance issued

## (d) What would push the value higher?

The guidance ceiling at the upper end is $92.8 billion (representing the +2% margin). Wall Street's consensus estimate is $91.9 billion, falling within the guided range. Given Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion and the 11% sequential growth implied by the $91B guidance, the range reflects realistic expectations.

The guidance was intentionally conservative, not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China, which could be a source of upside.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 revenue: $81.6 billion (up 20% sequentially, 85% YoY)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0 billion ±2% (11% sequential growth)
- Wall Street consensus: $91.9 billion
- Data Center revenue in Q1: $75.2 billion

The guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center revenue, suggesting potential conservatism.

---

## Reasoning

This question asks for the forward guidance that will be issued in NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release. However, the research clearly indicates that this guidance was **already issued on May 20, 2026** at **$91.0 billion ±2%** (range: $89.2B to $92.8B).

Since we are currently on August 23, 2026, and this guidance was announced over three months ago, the answer should be the official guidance that was provided: **$91.0 billion**.

The guidance falls comfortably within the provided range (99.5B to 115.5B is the full scale, though with open bounds). The actual guidance is well below the upper end of this forecasting range, reflecting a more conservative guidance typical of NVIDIA given the uncertainties around China revenues and market saturation concerns.

My estimate centers on the official $91.0 billion guidance with acknowledgment that the actual reported ceiling could reasonably be anywhere from $89.2B to $92.8B depending on how conservatively they chose to guide.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This range puts the ceiling near $92.8 billion and the floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

For comparison, Wall Street analysts' average estimate is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's projected range. NVIDIA reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion, up 20% sequentially and 85% year-over-year, with Data Center revenue at $75.2 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). The Q2 guidance of $91 billion implies an 11% sequential growth from Q1, a slowdown from the 20% sequential growth seen in Q1 [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
